Updated assessment incorporating the July 2021 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS):
- Credit supply and demand are more supportive than the FSR-only lens suggested. Banks reported stronger demand for C&I loans from large, middle-market, and small firms, along with higher borrower inquiries. Foreign banks also saw stronger C&I demand, tied to financing needs for inventories, receivables, capex, and M&A.
- Banks eased standards and terms for C&I and key consumer loan categories (credit cards, auto, and other consumer loans). Reasons cited included improved economic outlook, strong liquidity and capital positions, competition, and reduced perceived risk—consistent with the FOMC’s view that financial conditions are accommodative and credit is flowing to households and businesses.
- While some standards remained tighter than 2019 for certain segments, SLOOS broadly corroborates ongoing easing and credit availability, which offsets part of the vulnerability concerns flagged in the FSR (elevated valuations, nonbank fragilities, CRE/CMBS pockets).

Net effect: relative to the prior FSR-tempered read, SLOOS tilts the assessment more positive. The statement’s supportive stance plus evidence of easier bank lending move the tone from mildly positive/near-neutral to clearly but moderately positive.

sentiment score = 0.30
